summary: German legal theorist Carl Schmitt turned Weimar-era critiques of liberal democracy into a blueprint for destroying it, joined the Nazi Party in 1933, justified Hitler's purges and antisemitic laws, and later inspired far-right thinkers worldwide.

evidence.note: born July 1888 into a Catholic family in Plettenberg
long segment on Bismarck's Kulturkampf and Catholic marginalisation shaping him
settles in Strasbourg (then German, now France) for his doctorate under von Calker
Jewish friend Fritz Eisler and his family fund Schmitt for years
meets the dancer Cari, a con artist with an invented noble past, whom he marries
Eisler killed by shrapnel early in the First World War
1919 Political Romanticism, his first influential book; used as main_span start
Crisis of Parliamentary Democracy: homogeneity and exclusion as tools against liberalism
joins the Nazi Party in 1933 and drafts the case for expelling Jewish intellectuals
justifies the Night of the Long Knives; 1936 conference on purging Jewish influence
SS attack in December 1936 ends his influence; used as main_span end
postwar exile in Plettenberg, death in 1985, influence on Le Pen, Dugin, Strauss, Vance

notes: Primary fascism-far-right (taxonomy lists Schmitt as its example); nazism secondary for his 1933-36 party role. Eisler's birth year is not in the packet, left null. Cari's real dates are unknown, floruit 1912 when they meet. Legacy segment (French, Russian, US far right) sets reaches_present rather than adding settings. Setting FR is Strasbourg, German at the time. main_span could arguably run to the 1947 Nuremberg interrogations.
